text2activity_extraction_model.title: Response to passenger ship main engine cooling system failure

source_units.text: The passenger ship operation system consists of the bridge, 2 main engines, 2 generators, the engine monitoring system (EMS), and 4 lifeboats. The EMS monitors the coolant temperature of the main engines.
Externally there are the Coast Guard and the shipping company operations office; the captain is in charge of ship command, and the chief engineer is in charge of engine maintenance.

At 4:00 p.m., the EMS detects a coolant temperature of 95 °C on main engine No. 1 and displays an alarm on the bridge. The captain stops main engine No. 1 and operates at reduced speed with main engine No. 2 only.
The chief engineer inspects the coolant pump and confirms damage to the pump impeller. The chief engineer requests parts supply from the shipping company operations office.
The captain makes a reduced-speed operation announcement to the passengers and notifies the Coast Guard of the engine failure situation. The two tasks are carried out simultaneously.
If the load of main engine No. 2 is 85% or more, the chief engineer stops 1 generator to reduce the load. At 5:00 p.m., when the load rises to 88%, the chief engineer stops generator No. 2.
Every 30 min, the chief engineer reports the temperature and load of main engine No. 2 to the bridge.
If even main engine No. 2 stops, the captain requests towing from the Coast Guard. On this day, main engine No. 2 did not stop, so towing was not requested.
At 7:00 p.m., when the passenger ship enters the destination port, the shipping company operations office delivers the replacement impeller to the ship.

The chief engineer replaces the impeller and test-runs main engine No. 1. If the coolant temperature stays at 80 °C or less during the test run, the chief engineer reports repair completion to the captain.
The captain instructs that generator No. 2 be restarted and notifies the Coast Guard of the end of the situation.
The captain compiles the details of the engine failure and reports them to the shipping company operations office.
The goal of this scenario is to enter the scheduled port while keeping the passengers safe.
